content.latin: Veníte, exsultémus Dómino, iubilémus Deo, salutári nostro: præoccupémus fáciem eius in confessióne, et in psalmis iubilémus ei.
content.english: Come let us praise the Lord with joy: let us joyfully sing to God our saviour. Let us come before his presence with thanksgiving; and make a joyful noise to him with psalms.

content.latin: Ant. Regem Vírginum Dóminum, * Veníte, adorémus.
content.english: Ant. The Lord, the King of Virgins, * O come, let us worship.

segments.t: Ant.
Regem Vírginum Dóminum, * Veníte, adorémus.

content.latin: Quóniam Deus magnus Dóminus, et Rex magnus super omnes deos, quóniam non repéllet Dóminus plebem suam: quia in manu eius sunt omnes fines terræ, et altitúdines móntium ipse cónspicit.
content.english: For the Lord is a great God, and a great King above all gods. For the Lord will not cast off his people: for in his hand are all the ends of the earth, and the heights of the mountains are his.

content.latin: Ant. Veníte, adorémus.
content.english: Ant. O come, let us worship.

segments.t: Ant.
Veníte, adorémus.

content.latin: Quóniam ipsíus est mare, et ipse fecit illud, et áridam fundavérunt manus eius (genuflectitur) veníte, adorémus, et procidámus ante Deum: plorémus coram Dómino, qui fecit nos, quia ipse est Dóminus, Deus noster; nos autem pópulus eius, et oves páscuæ eius.
content.english: For the sea is his, and he made it: and his hands formed the dry land. (genuflect) Come let us adore and fall down: and weep before the Lord that made us: For he is the Lord our God: and we are the people of his pasture and the sheep of his hand.

segments.t: Quóniam ipsíus est mare, et ipse fecit illud, et áridam fundavérunt manus eius
(genuflectitur)
veníte, adorémus, et procidámus ante Deum: plorémus coram Dómino, qui fecit nos, quia ipse est Dóminus, Deus noster; nos autem pópulus eius, et oves páscuæ eius.

content.english: Ant. The Lord, the King of Virgins, * O come, let us worship.

segments.t: Ant.
Regem Vírginum Dóminum, * Veníte, adorémus.

content.latin: Hódie, si vocem eius audiéritis, nolíte obduráre corda vestra, sicut in exacerbatióne secúndum diem tentatiónis in desérto: ubi tentavérunt me patres vestri, probavérunt et vidérunt ópera mea.
content.english: Today if you shall hear his voice, harden not your hearts: As in the provocation, according to the day of temptation in the wilderness: where your fathers tempted me, they proved me, and saw my works.

content.latin: Ant. Veníte, adorémus.
content.english: Ant. O come, let us worship.

segments.t: Ant.
Veníte, adorémus.

content.latin: Quadragínta annis próximus fui generatióni huic, et dixi: Semper hi errant corde, ipsi vero non cognovérunt vias meas: quibus iurávi in ira mea: Si introíbunt in réquiem meam.
content.english: Forty years long was I offended with that generation, and I said: These always err in heart. And these men have not known my ways: so I swore in my wrath that they shall not enter into my rest.

content.latin: Vírginis Proles Opiféxque Matris,
content.english: Son of a virgin, maker of thy mother,

content.latin: Virgo quem gessit, peperítque Virgo:
content.english: Thou, rod and blossom from a stem unstainèd,

content.latin: Vírginis partos cánimus decóra
content.english: While we a Virgin's triumphs are rehearsing,

content.latin: Morte triúmphos.
content.english: Hear our petition!

content.latin: Hæc enim palmæ dúplicis beáta
content.english: Lo, on thy handmaid fell a two-fold blessing,

content.latin: Sorte, dum gestit frágilem domáre
content.english: Who, in her body vanquishing the weakness,

content.latin: Córporis sexum, dómuit cruéntum
content.english: In that same body, grace from heaven obtaining,

content.latin: Cæde tyránnum.
content.english: Bore the world witness.

content.latin: Unde nec mortem, nec amíca mortis
content.english: Death, nor the rending pains of death appalled her;

content.latin: Mille pœnárum génera expavéscens,
content.english: Bondage and torment found her undefeated:

content.latin: Sánguine effúso méruit serénum
content.english: So by the shedding of her blood attained she

content.latin: Scándere cælum.
content.english: Heavenly guerdon.

content.latin: Huius orátu, Deus alme, nobis
content.english: Fountain of mercy, hear the prayers she offers;

content.latin: Débitas pœnas scélerum remítte;
content.english: Purge our offences, pardon our transgressions,

content.latin: Ut tibi puro resonémus almum
content.english: So that hereafter we to thee may render

content.latin: Péctore carmen.
content.english: Praise with thanksgiving.

content.latin: Sit decus Patri, genitǽque Proli,
content.english: Thou, the All-Father, thou, the One-Begotten,

content.latin: Et tibi, compar utriúsque virtus,
content.english: Thou, Holy Spirit, Three in One co-equal,

content.latin: Spíritus semper, Deus unus, omni
content.english: Glory be henceforth thine through all the ages,

content.latin: Témporis ævo.
content.english: World without ending.

content.latin: Amen.
content.english: Amen.

content.latin: Ant. Speciósus forma * præ fíliis hóminum, diffúsa est grátia in lábiis tuis.
content.english: Ant. Thou art beautiful * above the sons of men: grace is poured abroad in thy lips.

segments.t: Ant.
Speciósus forma * præ fíliis hóminum, diffúsa est grátia in lábiis tuis.

content.latin: Psalmus 44(2a-10b) [1]

segments.t: Psalmus 44(2a-10b)

content.latin: 44:2 Eructávit cor meum verbum bonum: * dico ego ópera mea Regi.
content.english: 44:2 My heart hath uttered a good word; * I speak my works to the King.

segments.t: Eructávit cor meum verbum bonum: * dico ego ópera mea Regi.

content.latin: 44:2 Lingua mea cálamus scribæ: * velóciter scribéntis.
content.english: 44:2 My tongue is the pen of a scrivener * that writeth swiftly.

segments.t: Lingua mea cálamus scribæ: * velóciter scribéntis.

content.latin: 44:3 Speciósus forma præ fíliis hóminum, diffúsa est grátia in lábiis tuis: * proptérea benedíxit te Deus in ætérnum.
content.english: 44:3 Thou art beautiful above the sons of men: grace is poured abroad in thy lips; * therefore hath God blessed thee for ever.

segments.t: Speciósus forma præ fíliis hóminum, diffúsa est grátia in lábiis tuis: * proptérea benedíxit te Deus in ætérnum.

content.latin: 44:4 Accíngere gládio tuo super femur tuum, * potentíssime.
content.english: 44:4 Gird thy sword upon thy thigh, * O thou most mighty.

segments.t: Accíngere gládio tuo super femur tuum, * potentíssime.

content.latin: 44:5 Spécie tua et pulchritúdine tua: * inténde, próspere procéde, et regna.
content.english: 44:5 With thy comeliness and thy beauty * set out, proceed prosperously, and reign.

segments.t: Spécie tua et pulchritúdine tua: * inténde, próspere procéde, et regna.

content.latin: 44:5 Propter veritátem, et mansuetúdinem, et iustítiam: * et dedúcet te mirabíliter déxtera tua.
content.english: 44:5 Because of truth and meekness and justice: * and thy right hand shall conduct thee wonderfully.

segments.t: Propter veritátem, et mansuetúdinem, et iustítiam: * et dedúcet te mirabíliter déxtera tua.

content.latin: 44:6 Sagíttæ tuæ acútæ, pópuli sub te cadent: * in corda inimicórum Regis.
content.english: 44:6 Thy arrows are sharp: under thee shall people fall, * into the hearts of the king’s enemies.

segments.t: Sagíttæ tuæ acútæ, pópuli sub te cadent: * in corda inimicórum Regis.

content.latin: 44:7 Sedes tua, Deus, in sǽculum sǽculi: * virga directiónis virga regni tui.
content.english: 44:7 Thy throne, O God, is for ever and ever: * the sceptre of thy kingdom is a sceptre of uprightness.

segments.t: Sedes tua, Deus, in sǽculum sǽculi: * virga directiónis virga regni tui.

content.latin: 44:8 Dilexísti iustítiam, et odísti iniquitátem: * proptérea unxit te Deus, Deus tuus, óleo lætítiæ præ consórtibus tuis.
content.english: 44:8 Thou hast loved justice, and hated iniquity: * therefore God, thy God, hath anointed thee with the oil of gladness above thy fellows.

segments.t: Dilexísti iustítiam, et odísti iniquitátem: * proptérea unxit te Deus, Deus tuus, óleo lætítiæ præ consórtibus tuis.

content.latin: 44:9 Myrrha, et gutta, et cásia a vestiméntis tuis, a dómibus ebúrneis: * ex quibus delectavérunt te fíliæ regum in honóre tuo.
content.english: 44:9 Myrrh and stacte and cassia perfume thy garments, from the ivory houses: * out of which the daughters of kings have delighted thee in thy glory.

segments.t: Myrrha, et gutta, et cásia a vestiméntis tuis, a dómibus ebúrneis: * ex quibus delectavérunt te fíliæ regum in honóre tuo.

content.latin: 44:10 Ástitit regína a dextris tuis in vestítu deauráto: * circúmdata varietáte.
content.english: 44:10 The queen stood on thy right hand, in gilded clothing; * surrounded with variety.

segments.t: Ástitit regína a dextris tuis in vestítu deauráto: * circúmdata varietáte.

content.latin: Psalmus 44(11-18b) [2]

segments.t: Psalmus 44(11-18b)

content.latin: 44:11 Audi fília, et vide, et inclína aurem tuam: * et oblivíscere pópulum tuum et domum patris tui.
content.english: 44:11 Hearken, O daughter, and see, and incline thy ear: * and forget thy people and thy father’s house.

segments.t: Audi fília, et vide, et inclína aurem tuam: * et oblivíscere pópulum tuum et domum patris tui.

content.latin: 44:12 Et concupíscet Rex decórem tuum: * quóniam ipse est Dóminus Deus tuus, et adorábunt eum.
content.english: 44:12 And the king shall greatly desire thy beauty; * for he is the Lord thy God, and him they shall adore.

segments.t: Et concupíscet Rex decórem tuum: * quóniam ipse est Dóminus Deus tuus, et adorábunt eum.

content.latin: 44:13 Et fíliæ Tyri in munéribus * vultum tuum deprecabúntur: omnes dívites plebis.
content.english: 44:13 And the daughters of Tyre with gifts, * yea, all the rich among the people, shall entreat thy countenance.

segments.t: Et fíliæ Tyri in munéribus * vultum tuum deprecabúntur: omnes dívites plebis.

content.latin: 44:14 Omnis glória eius fíliæ Regis ab intus, * in fímbriis áureis circumamícta varietátibus.
content.english: 44:14 All the glory of the king’s daughter is within, * in golden borders, clothed round about with varieties.

segments.t: Omnis glória eius fíliæ Regis ab intus, * in fímbriis áureis circumamícta varietátibus.

content.latin: 44:15 Adducéntur Regi vírgines post eam: * próximæ eius afferéntur tibi.
content.english: 44:15 After her shall virgins be brought to the king: * her neighbours shall be brought to thee.

segments.t: Adducéntur Regi vírgines post eam: * próximæ eius afferéntur tibi.

content.latin: 44:16 Afferéntur in lætítia et exsultatióne: * adducéntur in templum Regis.
content.english: 44:16 They shall be brought with gladness and rejoicing: * they shall be brought into the temple of the king.

segments.t: Afferéntur in lætítia et exsultatióne: * adducéntur in templum Regis.

content.latin: 44:17 Pro pátribus tuis nati sunt tibi fílii: * constítues eos príncipes super omnem terram.
content.english: 44:17 Instead of thy fathers, sons are born to thee: * thou shalt make them princes over all the earth.

segments.t: Pro pátribus tuis nati sunt tibi fílii: * constítues eos príncipes super omnem terram.

content.latin: 44:18 Mémores erunt nóminis tui: * in omni generatióne et generatiónem.
content.english: 44:18 They shall remember thy name * throughout all generations.

segments.t: Mémores erunt nóminis tui: * in omni generatióne et generatiónem.

content.latin: 44:18 Proptérea pópuli confitebúntur tibi in ætérnum: * et in sǽculum sǽculi.
content.english: 44:18 Therefore shall people praise thee for ever; yea, * for ever and ever.

segments.t: Proptérea pópuli confitebúntur tibi in ætérnum: * et in sǽculum sǽculi.

content.latin: Psalmus 45 [3]
content.english: Psalm 45 [3]

segments.t: Psalmus 45

content.latin: 45:2 Deus noster refúgium, et virtus: * adiútor in tribulatiónibus, quæ invenérunt nos nimis.
content.english: 45:2 Our God is our refuge and strength: * a helper in troubles, which have found us exceedingly.

segments.t: Deus noster refúgium, et virtus: * adiútor in tribulatiónibus, quæ invenérunt nos nimis.

content.latin: 45:3 Proptérea non timébimus dum turbábitur terra: * et transferéntur montes in cor maris.
content.english: 45:3 Therefore we will not fear, when the earth shall be troubled; * and the mountains shall be removed into the heart of the sea.

segments.t: Proptérea non timébimus dum turbábitur terra: * et transferéntur montes in cor maris.

content.latin: 45:4 Sonuérunt, et turbátæ sunt aquæ eórum: * conturbáti sunt montes in fortitúdine eius.
content.english: 45:4 Their waters roared and were troubled: * the mountains were troubled with his strength.

segments.t: Sonuérunt, et turbátæ sunt aquæ eórum: * conturbáti sunt montes in fortitúdine eius.

content.latin: 45:5 Flúminis ímpetus lætíficat civitátem Dei: * sanctificávit tabernáculum suum Altíssimus.
content.english: 45:5 The stream of the river maketh the city of God joyful: * the most High hath sanctified his own tabernacle.

segments.t: Flúminis ímpetus lætíficat civitátem Dei: * sanctificávit tabernáculum suum Altíssimus.

content.latin: 45:6 Deus in médio eius, non commovébitur: * adiuvábit eam Deus mane dilúculo.
content.english: 45:6 God is in the midst thereof, it shall not be moved: * God will help it in the morning early.

segments.t: Deus in médio eius, non commovébitur: * adiuvábit eam Deus mane dilúculo.

content.latin: 45:7 Conturbátæ sunt gentes, et inclináta sunt regna: * dedit vocem suam, mota est terra.
content.english: 45:7 Nations were troubled, and kingdoms were bowed down: * he uttered his voice, the earth trembled.

segments.t: Conturbátæ sunt gentes, et inclináta sunt regna: * dedit vocem suam, mota est terra.

content.latin: 45:8 Dóminus virtútum nobíscum: * suscéptor noster Deus Iacob.
content.english: 45:8 The Lord of armies is with us: * the God of Jacob is our protector.

segments.t: Dóminus virtútum nobíscum: * suscéptor noster Deus Iacob.

content.latin: 45:9 Veníte, et vidéte ópera Dómini, quæ pósuit prodígia super terram: * áuferens bella usque ad finem terræ.
content.english: 45:9 Come and behold ye the works of the Lord: what wonders he hath done upon earth, * making wars to cease even to the end of the earth.

segments.t: Veníte, et vidéte ópera Dómini, quæ pósuit prodígia super terram: * áuferens bella usque ad finem terræ.

content.latin: 45:10 Arcum cónteret, et confrínget arma: * et scuta combúret igni.
content.english: 45:10 He shall destroy the bow, and break the weapons: * and the shield he shall burn in the fire.

segments.t: Arcum cónteret, et confrínget arma: * et scuta combúret igni.

content.latin: 45:11 Vacáte, et vidéte quóniam ego sum Deus: * exaltábor in géntibus, et exaltábor in terra.
content.english: 45:11 Be still and see that I am God; * I will be exalted among the nations, and I will be exalted in the earth.

segments.t: Vacáte, et vidéte quóniam ego sum Deus: * exaltábor in géntibus, et exaltábor in terra.

content.latin: 47:2 Magnus Dóminus, et laudábilis nimis in civitáte Dei nostri, ‡ in monte sancto eius.
content.english: 47:2 Great is the Lord, and exceedingly to be praised in the city of our God, ‡ in his holy mountain.

content.latin: 47:3 Fundátur exsultatióne univérsæ terræ mons Sion, * látera Aquilónis, cívitas Regis magni.
content.english: 47:3 With the joy of the whole earth is mount Sion founded, * on the sides of the north, the city of the great king.

segments.t: Fundátur exsultatióne univérsæ terræ mons Sion, * látera Aquilónis, cívitas Regis magni.

content.latin: 47:4 Deus in dómibus eius cognoscétur: * cum suscípiet eam.
content.english: 47:4 In her houses shall God be known, * when he shall protect her.

segments.t: Deus in dómibus eius cognoscétur: * cum suscípiet eam.

content.latin: 47:5 Quóniam ecce reges terræ congregáti sunt: * convenérunt in unum.
content.english: 47:5 For behold the kings of the earth assembled themselves: * they gathered together.

segments.t: Quóniam ecce reges terræ congregáti sunt: * convenérunt in unum.

content.latin: 47:6 Ipsi vidéntes sic admiráti sunt, conturbáti sunt, commóti sunt: * tremor apprehéndit eos.
content.english: 47:6 So they saw, and they wondered, they were troubled, they were moved: * trembling took hold of them.

segments.t: Ipsi vidéntes sic admiráti sunt, conturbáti sunt, commóti sunt: * tremor apprehéndit eos.

content.latin: 47:7 Ibi dolóres ut parturiéntis: * in spíritu veheménti cónteres naves Tharsis.
content.english: 47:7 There were pains as of a woman in labour; * with a vehement wind thou shalt break in pieces the ships of Tharsis.

segments.t: Ibi dolóres ut parturiéntis: * in spíritu veheménti cónteres naves Tharsis.

content.latin: 47:9 Sicut audívimus, sic vídimus in civitáte Dómini virtútum, in civitáte Dei nostri: * Deus fundávit eam in ætérnum.
content.english: 47:9 As we have heard, so have we seen, in the city of the Lord of hosts, in the city of our God: * God hath founded it for ever.

segments.t: Sicut audívimus, sic vídimus in civitáte Dómini virtútum, in civitáte Dei nostri: * Deus fundávit eam in ætérnum.

content.latin: 47:10 Suscépimus, Deus, misericórdiam tuam, * in médio templi tui.
content.english: 47:10 We have received thy mercy, O God, * in the midst of thy temple.

segments.t: Suscépimus, Deus, misericórdiam tuam, * in médio templi tui.

content.latin: 47:11 Secúndum nomen tuum, Deus, sic et laus tua in fines terræ: * iustítia plena est déxtera tua.
content.english: 47:11 According to thy name, O God, so also is thy praise unto the ends of the earth: * thy right hand is full of justice.

segments.t: Secúndum nomen tuum, Deus, sic et laus tua in fines terræ: * iustítia plena est déxtera tua.

content.latin: 47:12 Lætétur mons Sion, et exsúltent fíliæ Iudæ: * propter iudícia tua, Dómine.
content.english: 47:12 Let mount Sion rejoice, and the daughters of Juda be glad; * because of thy judgments, O Lord.

segments.t: Lætétur mons Sion, et exsúltent fíliæ Iudæ: * propter iudícia tua, Dómine.

content.latin: 47:13 Circúmdate Sion, et complectímini eam: * narráte in túrribus eius.
content.english: 47:13 Surround Sion, and encompass her: * tell ye in her towers.

segments.t: Circúmdate Sion, et complectímini eam: * narráte in túrribus eius.

content.latin: 47:14 Pónite corda vestra in virtúte eius: * et distribúite domos eius, ut enarrétis in progénie áltera.
content.english: 47:14 Set your hearts on her strength; and distribute her houses, * that ye may relate it in another generation.

segments.t: Pónite corda vestra in virtúte eius: * et distribúite domos eius, ut enarrétis in progénie áltera.

content.latin: 47:15 Quóniam hic est Deus, Deus noster in ætérnum et in sǽculum sǽculi: * ipse reget nos in sǽcula.
content.english: 47:15 For this is God, our God unto eternity, and for ever and ever: * he shall rule us for evermore.

segments.t: Quóniam hic est Deus, Deus noster in ætérnum et in sǽculum sǽculi: * ipse reget nos in sǽcula.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

segments.t: Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

segments.t: Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.

content.latin: Ant. Magnus Dóminus et laudábilis nimis in civitáte Dei nostri.
content.english: Ant. Great is the Lord and exceedingly to be praised in the city of our God.

segments.t: Ant.
Magnus Dóminus et laudábilis nimis in civitáte Dei nostri.

content.latin: Ant. Os meum loquétur * sapiéntiam: et meditátio cordis mei prudéntiam.
content.english: Ant. My mouth shall speak * wisdom: and the meditation of my heart understanding.

segments.t: Ant.
Os meum loquétur * sapiéntiam: et meditátio cordis mei prudéntiam.
Psalmus 48(2-13)

content.latin: 48:2 Audíte hæc, omnes gentes: * áuribus percípite omnes, qui habitátis orbem:
content.english: 48:2 Hear these things, all ye nations: * give ear, all ye inhabitants of the world.

segments.t: Audíte hæc, omnes gentes: * áuribus percípite omnes, qui habitátis orbem:

content.latin: 48:3 Quique terrígenæ, et fílii hóminum: * simul in unum dives et pauper.
content.english: 48:3 All you that are earthborn, and you sons of men: * both rich and poor together.

segments.t: Quique terrígenæ, et fílii hóminum: * simul in unum dives et pauper.

content.latin: 48:4 Os meum loquétur sapiéntiam: * et meditátio cordis mei prudéntiam.
content.english: 48:4 My mouth shall speak wisdom: * and the meditation of my heart understanding

segments.t: Os meum loquétur sapiéntiam: * et meditátio cordis mei prudéntiam.

content.latin: 48:5 Inclinábo in parábolam aurem meam: * apériam in psaltério propositiónem meam.
content.english: 48:5 I will incline my ear to a parable; * I will open my proposition on the psaltery.

segments.t: Inclinábo in parábolam aurem meam: * apériam in psaltério propositiónem meam.

content.latin: 48:6 Cur timébo in die mala? * iníquitas calcánei mei circúmdabit me:
content.english: 48:6 Why shall I fear in the evil day? * the iniquity of my heel shall encompass me.

segments.t: Cur timébo in die mala? * iníquitas calcánei mei circúmdabit me:

content.latin: 48:7 Qui confídunt in virtúte sua: * et in multitúdine divitiárum suárum gloriántur.
content.english: 48:7 They that trust in their own strength, * and glory in the multitude of their riches,

segments.t: Qui confídunt in virtúte sua: * et in multitúdine divitiárum suárum gloriántur.

content.latin: 48:8 Frater non rédimit, rédimet homo: * non dabit Deo placatiónem suam.
content.english: 48:8 No brother can redeem, nor shall man redeem: * he shall not give to God his ransom,

segments.t: Frater non rédimit, rédimet homo: * non dabit Deo placatiónem suam.

content.latin: 48:9 Et prétium redemptiónis ánimæ suæ: * et laborábit in ætérnum, et vivet adhuc in finem.
content.english: 48:9 Nor the price of the redemption of his soul: * and shall labour for ever, and shall still live unto the end.

segments.t: Et prétium redemptiónis ánimæ suæ: * et laborábit in ætérnum, et vivet adhuc in finem.

content.latin: 48:11 Non vidébit intéritum, cum víderit sapiéntes moriéntes: * simul insípiens, et stultus períbunt.
content.english: 48:11 He shall not see destruction, when he shall see the wise dying: * the senseless and the fool shall perish together:

segments.t: Non vidébit intéritum, cum víderit sapiéntes moriéntes: * simul insípiens, et stultus períbunt.

content.latin: 48:11 Et relínquent aliénis divítias suas: * et sepúlcra eórum domus illórum in ætérnum.
content.english: 48:11 And they shall leave their riches to strangers: * and their sepulchres shall be their houses for ever.

segments.t: Et relínquent aliénis divítias suas: * et sepúlcra eórum domus illórum in ætérnum.

content.latin: 48:12 Tabernácula eórum in progénie et progénie: * vocavérunt nómina sua in terris suis.
content.english: 48:12 Their dwelling places to all generations: * they have called their lands by their names.

segments.t: Tabernácula eórum in progénie et progénie: * vocavérunt nómina sua in terris suis.

content.latin: 48:13 Et homo, cum in honóre esset, non intelléxit: * comparátus est iuméntis insipiéntibus, et símilis factus est illis.
content.english: 48:13 And man when he was in honour did not understand; * he is compared to senseless beasts, and is become like to them.

segments.t: Et homo, cum in honóre esset, non intelléxit: * comparátus est iuméntis insipiéntibus, et símilis factus est illis.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

segments.t: Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

segments.t: Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.

content.latin: Ant. Os meum loquétur sapiéntiam: et meditátio cordis mei prudéntiam.
content.english: Ant. My mouth shall speak wisdom: and the meditation of my heart understanding.

segments.t: Ant.
Os meum loquétur sapiéntiam: et meditátio cordis mei prudéntiam.

content.latin: Ant. Ne timúeris * cum dívite non descéndet in sepúlcrum glória eius.
content.english: Ant. Be not thou afraid * the things which made him rich, or his glory shall not descend with him to the sepulchre.

segments.t: Ant.
Ne timúeris * cum dívite non descéndet in sepúlcrum glória eius.
Psalmus 48(14-21)

content.latin: 48:14 Hæc via illórum scándalum ipsis: * et póstea in ore suo complacébunt.
content.english: 48:14 This way of theirs is a stumbling block to them: * and afterwards they shall delight in their mouth.

segments.t: Hæc via illórum scándalum ipsis: * et póstea in ore suo complacébunt.

content.latin: 48:15 Sicut oves in inférno pósiti sunt: * mors depáscet eos.
content.english: 48:15 They are laid in hell like sheep: * death shall feed upon them.

segments.t: Sicut oves in inférno pósiti sunt: * mors depáscet eos.

content.latin: 48:15 Et dominabúntur eórum iusti in matutíno: * et auxílium eórum veteráscet in inférno a glória eórum.
content.english: 48:15 And the just shall have dominion over them in the morning; * and their help shall decay in hell from their glory.

segments.t: Et dominabúntur eórum iusti in matutíno: * et auxílium eórum veteráscet in inférno a glória eórum.

content.latin: 48:16 Verúmtamen Deus rédimet ánimam meam de manu ínferi: * cum accéperit me.
content.english: 48:16 But God will redeem my soul from the hand of hell, * when he shall receive me.

segments.t: Verúmtamen Deus rédimet ánimam meam de manu ínferi: * cum accéperit me.

content.latin: 48:17 Ne timúeris, cum dives factus fúerit homo: * et cum multiplicáta fúerit glória domus eius.
content.english: 48:17 Be not thou afraid, when a man shall be made rich, * and when the glory of his house shall be increased.

segments.t: Ne timúeris, cum dives factus fúerit homo: * et cum multiplicáta fúerit glória domus eius.

content.latin: 48:18 Quóniam cum interíerit, non sumet ómnia: * neque descéndet cum eo glória eius.
content.english: 48:18 For when he shall die he shall take nothing away; * nor shall his glory descend with him.

segments.t: Quóniam cum interíerit, non sumet ómnia: * neque descéndet cum eo glória eius.

content.latin: 48:19 Quia ánima eius in vita ipsíus benedicétur: * confitébitur tibi cum beneféceris ei.
content.english: 48:19 For in his lifetime his soul will be blessed: * and he will praise thee when thou shalt do well to him.

segments.t: Quia ánima eius in vita ipsíus benedicétur: * confitébitur tibi cum beneféceris ei.

content.latin: 48:20 Introíbit usque in progénies patrum suórum: * et usque in ætérnum non vidébit lumen.
content.english: 48:20 He shall go in to the generations of his fathers: * and he shall never see light.

segments.t: Introíbit usque in progénies patrum suórum: * et usque in ætérnum non vidébit lumen.

content.latin: 48:21 Homo, cum in honóre esset, non intelléxit: * comparátus est iuméntis insipiéntibus, et símilis factus est illis.
content.english: 48:21 Man when he was in honour did not understand: * he hath been compared to senseless beasts, and made like to them.

segments.t: Homo, cum in honóre esset, non intelléxit: * comparátus est iuméntis insipiéntibus, et símilis factus est illis.

content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

segments.t: Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.

content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

segments.t: Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.

content.latin: Ant. Ne timúeris cum dívite non descéndet in sepúlcrum glória eius.
content.english: Ant. Be not thou afraid the things which made him rich, or his glory shall not descend with him to the sepulchre.

segments.t: Ant.
Ne timúeris cum dívite non descéndet in sepúlcrum glória eius.

content.latin: Ant. Deus deórum, * Dóminus locútus est. ‡
content.english: Ant. The God of gods, * the Lord hath spoken. ‡

segments.t: Ant.
Deus deórum, * Dóminus locútus est.
Psalmus 49(1-15)

content.latin: 49:1 Deus deórum, Dóminus locútus est: * ‡ et vocávit terram,
content.english: 49:1 The God of gods, the Lord hath spoken: * ‡ and he hath called the earth.

segments.t: Deus deórum, Dóminus locútus est: *
et vocávit terram,

content.latin: 49:1 A solis ortu usque ad occásum: * ex Sion spécies decóris eius.
content.english: 49:1 From the rising of the sun, to the going down thereof: * out of Sion the loveliness of his beauty.

segments.t: A solis ortu usque ad occásum: * ex Sion spécies decóris eius.

content.latin: 49:3 Deus maniféste véniet: * Deus noster et non silébit.
content.english: 49:3 God shall come manifestly: our God shall come, * and shall not keep silence.

segments.t: Deus maniféste véniet: * Deus noster et non silébit.

content.latin: 49:3 Ignis in conspéctu eius exardéscet: * et in circúitu eius tempéstas válida.
content.english: 49:3 A fire shall burn before him: * and a mighty tempest shall be round about

segments.t: Ignis in conspéctu eius exardéscet: * et in circúitu eius tempéstas válida.

content.latin: 49:4 Advocábit cælum desúrsum: * et terram discérnere pópulum suum.
content.english: 49:4 He shall call heaven from above, * and the earth, to judge his people.

segments.t: Advocábit cælum desúrsum: * et terram discérnere pópulum suum.

content.latin: 49:5 Congregáte illi sanctos eius: * qui órdinant testaméntum eius super sacrifícia.
content.english: 49:5 Gather ye together his saints to him: * who set his covenant before sacrifices.

segments.t: Congregáte illi sanctos eius: * qui órdinant testaméntum eius super sacrifícia.

content.latin: 49:6 Et annuntiábunt cæli iustítiam eius: * quóniam Deus iudex est.
content.english: 49:6 And the heavens shall declare his justice: * for God is judge.

segments.t: Et annuntiábunt cæli iustítiam eius: * quóniam Deus iudex est.

content.latin: 49:7 Audi, pópulus meus, et loquar: Israël, et testificábor tibi: * Deus, Deus tuus ego sum.
content.english: 49:7 Hear, O my people, and I will speak: O Israel, and I will testify to thee: * I am God, thy God.

segments.t: Audi, pópulus meus, et loquar: Israël, et testificábor tibi: * Deus, Deus tuus ego sum.

content.latin: 49:8 Non in sacrifíciis tuis árguam te: * holocáusta autem tua in conspéctu meo sunt semper.
content.english: 49:8 I will not reprove thee for thy sacrifices: * and thy burnt offerings are always in my sight.

segments.t: Non in sacrifíciis tuis árguam te: * holocáusta autem tua in conspéctu meo sunt semper.

content.latin: 49:9 Non accípiam de domo tua vítulos: * neque de grégibus tuis hircos.
content.english: 49:9 I will not take calves out of thy house: * nor he goats out of thy flocks.

segments.t: Non accípiam de domo tua vítulos: * neque de grégibus tuis hircos.

content.latin: 49:10 Quóniam meæ sunt omnes feræ silvárum: * iuménta in móntibus et boves.
content.english: 49:10 For all the beasts of the woods are mine: * the cattle on the hills, and the oxen.

segments.t: Quóniam meæ sunt omnes feræ silvárum: * iuménta in móntibus et boves.

content.latin: 49:11 Cognóvi ómnia volatília cæli: * et pulchritúdo agri mecum est.
content.english: 49:11 I know all the fowls of the air: * and with me is the beauty of the field.

segments.t: Cognóvi ómnia volatília cæli: * et pulchritúdo agri mecum est.

content.latin: 49:12 Si esuríero, non dicam tibi: * meus est enim orbis terræ, et plenitúdo eius.
content.english: 49:12 If I should be hungry, I would not tell thee: * for the world is mine, and the fulness thereof.

segments.t: Si esuríero, non dicam tibi: * meus est enim orbis terræ, et plenitúdo eius.

content.latin: 49:13 Numquid manducábo carnes taurórum? * aut sánguinem hircórum potábo?
content.english: 49:13 Shall I eat the flesh of bullocks? * or shall I drink the blood of goats?

segments.t: Numquid manducábo carnes taurórum? * aut sánguinem hircórum potábo?

content.latin: 49:14 Ímmola Deo sacrifícium laudis: * et redde Altíssimo vota tua.
content.english: 49:14 Offer to God the sacrifice of praise: * and pay thy vows to the most High.

segments.t: Ímmola Deo sacrifícium laudis: * et redde Altíssimo vota tua.

content.latin: 49:15 Et ínvoca me in die tribulatiónis: * éruam te, et honorificábis me.
content.english: 49:15 And call upon me in the day of trouble: * I will deliver thee, and thou shalt glorify me.

segments.t: Et ínvoca me in die tribulatiónis: * éruam te, et honorificábis me.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

segments.t: Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

segments.t: Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.

content.latin: Ant. Deus deórum, Dóminus locútus est.
content.english: Ant. The God of gods, the Lord hath spoken.

segments.t: Ant.
Deus deórum, Dóminus locútus est.

content.latin: Ant. Intellégite, * qui obliviscímini Deum.
content.english: Ant. Understand these things, * you that forget God.

segments.t: Ant.
Intellégite, * qui obliviscímini Deum.
Psalmus 49(16-23)

content.latin: 49:16 Peccatóri autem dixit Deus: * Quare tu enárras iustítias meas, et assúmis testaméntum meum per os tuum?
content.english: 49:16 But to the sinner God hath said: * Why dost thou declare my justices, and take my covenant in thy mouth?

segments.t: Peccatóri autem dixit Deus: * Quare tu enárras iustítias meas, et assúmis testaméntum meum per os tuum?

content.latin: 49:17 Tu vero odísti disciplínam: * et proiecísti sermónes meos retrórsum:
content.english: 49:17 Seeing thou hast hated discipline: * and hast cast my words behind thee.

segments.t: Tu vero odísti disciplínam: * et proiecísti sermónes meos retrórsum:

content.latin: 49:18 Si vidébas furem, currébas cum eo: * et cum adúlteris portiónem tuam ponébas.
content.english: 49:18 If thou didst see a thief thou didst run with him: * and with adulterers thou hast been a partaker.

segments.t: Si vidébas furem, currébas cum eo: * et cum adúlteris portiónem tuam ponébas.

content.latin: 49:19 Os tuum abundávit malítia: * et lingua tua concinnábat dolos.
content.english: 49:19 Thy mouth hath abounded with evil, * and thy tongue framed deceits.

segments.t: Os tuum abundávit malítia: * et lingua tua concinnábat dolos.

content.latin: 49:20 Sedens advérsus fratrem tuum loquebáris, et advérsus fílium matris tuæ ponébas scándalum: * hæc fecísti, et tácui.
content.english: 49:20 Sitting thou didst speak against thy brother, and didst lay a scandal against thy mother’s son: * these things hast thou done, and I was silent.

segments.t: Sedens advérsus fratrem tuum loquebáris, et advérsus fílium matris tuæ ponébas scándalum: * hæc fecísti, et tácui.

content.latin: 49:21 Existimásti, iníque, quod ero tui símilis: * árguam te, et státuam contra fáciem tuam.
content.english: 49:21 Thou thoughtest unjustly that I should be like to thee: * but I will reprove thee, and set before thy face.

segments.t: Existimásti, iníque, quod ero tui símilis: * árguam te, et státuam contra fáciem tuam.

content.latin: 49:22 Intellégite hæc, qui obliviscímini Deum: * nequándo rápiat, et non sit qui erípiat.
content.english: 49:22 Understand these things, you that forget God; * lest he snatch you away, and there be none to deliver you.

segments.t: Intellégite hæc, qui obliviscímini Deum: * nequándo rápiat, et non sit qui erípiat.

content.latin: 49:23 Sacrifícium laudis honorificábit me: * et illic iter, quo osténdam illi salutáre Dei.
content.english: 49:23 The sacrifice of praise shall glorify me: * and there is the way by which I will shew him the salvation of God.

segments.t: Sacrifícium laudis honorificábit me: * et illic iter, quo osténdam illi salutáre Dei.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

content.latin: Dum sǽculo quinto fere médio Attila Hunnórum dux a prima sua in Gállias irruptióne, ubi ad Cataláunum profligátus fúerat, in Pannóniam revertebátur, ántequam Rhenum traiíceret, nobilíssimam urbem Colóniam Agrippínam aggréditur, et ob ódium cathólicæ religiónis, quæ ibi máxime florébit, eam rapína ac cædibus vastábat. Sævíssimo autem ímpetu bárbari libídine æstuántes in vírgines puéllas irruébant, quæ a Británnia emigrántes ibídem commorabántur: inter quas præclaríssima éxstitit virgo Ursula nómine, quæ céteras hortabátur sócias, ómnia pótius subíre torménta mortémque crudelíssimam obíre, quam virginális pudicítiæ detriméntum pati. Cum nóbile hoc virgíneum agmen constantíssime Hunnis restitísset, partim ab ipsis gládio trucidátæ, partim sagíttis transfíxæ, partim véctibus contúsæ martýrium consummárunt. Ursula vero super cómitum suárum velut cæléstium margaritárum acérvum gloriósa víctima procúmbens, púrpura pro fide et castitáte fusi sánguinis decoráta, exércitum géminis virginitátis et fidei corónis insígnem in cælum triúmphans introdúxit. Postquam vero sæva barbarórum procélla deflúxit, Coloniénses supérstites Vírginum aliorúmque cívium mártyrum córpora ut pretiósa pígnora collegérunt, et summo honóre condidérunt. In agro virgíneo sánguine rubro, in quo sacra quies Martýribus data fuit, basílica ædificáta est, iam médio sǽculo séptimo sanctárum Vírginum dicta, ob quarum reveréntiam nullum exínde cadáver humánum illic tumulabátur. Quæ sǽculo nono monastérium facta, inítio décimi moniáles ob metum Hungarórum prófugas recépit, semper ab ínclitæ civitátis Præsúlibus liberáliter dotáta et pie visitáta. Conspiciúntur usque in hunc diem ecclésiæ sæpe restaurátæ muri Mártyrum lóculis úndique exornáti, dum maior reliquiárum pars intra chori paríetes et sub pavménto látitant; cernúntur in próximo oratório innúmera vírginum cápita, martýrii vestigíis partim insígnita, partim crínibus sanguinolén­tis tecta. Hæc sacra pígnora præterítis tempóribus piis peregrinatiónibus fidéles prosecutí sunt.
content.english: Dum sǽculo quinto fere médio Attila Hunnórum dux a prima sua in Gállias irruptióne, ubi ad Cataláunum profligátus fúerat, in Pannóniam revertebátur, ántequam Rhenum trajíceret, nobilíssimam urbem Colóniam Agrippínam aggréditur, et ob ódium cathólicæ religiónis, quæ ibi máxime florébit, eam rapína ac cædibus vastábat. Sævíssimo autem ímpetu bárbari libídine æstuántes in vírgines puéllas irruébant, quæ a Británnia emigrántes ibídem commorabántur: inter quas præclaríssima éxstitit virgo Ursula nómine, quæ céteras hortabátur sócias, ómnia pótius subíre torménta mortémque crudelíssimam obíre, quam virginális pudicítiæ detriméntum pati. Cum nóbile hoc virgíneum agmen constantíssime Hunnis restitísset, partim ab ipsis gládio trucidátæ, partim sagíttis transfíxæ, partim véctibus contúsæ martýrium consummárunt. Ursula vero super cómitum suárum velut cæléstium margaritárum acérvum gloriósa víctima procúmbens, púrpura pro fide et castitáte fusi sánguinis decoráta, exércitum géminis virginitátis et fidei corónis insígnem in cælum triúmphans introdúxit. Postquam vero sæva barbarórum procélla deflúxit, Coloniénses supérstites Vírginum aliorúmque cívium mártyrum córpora ut pretiósa pígnora collegérunt, et summo honóre condidérunt. In agro virgíneo sánguine rubro, in quo sacra quies Martýribus data fuit, basílica ædificáta est, jam médio sǽculo séptimo sanctárum Vírginum dicta, ob quarum reveréntiam nullum exínde cadáver humánum illic tumulabátur. Quæ sǽculo nono monastérium facta, inítio décimi moniáles ob metum Hungarórum prófugas recépit, semper ab ínclitæ civitátis Præsúlibus liberáliter dotáta et pie visitáta. Conspiciúntur usque in hunc diem ecclésiæ sæpe restaurátæ muri Mártyrum lóculis úndique exornáti, dum major reliquiárum pars intra chori paríetes et sub pavménto látitant; cernúntur in próximo oratório innúmera vírginum cápita, martýrii vestigíis partim insígnita, partim crínibus sanguinolén­tis tecta. Hæc sacra pígnora præterítis tempóribus piis peregrinatiónibus fidéles prosecutí sunt.

content.latin: 100:3 Non proponébam ante óculos meos rem iniústam: * faciéntes prævaricatiónes odívi.
content.english: 100:3 I did not set before my eyes any unjust thing: * I hated the workers of iniquities.

segments.t: Non proponébam ante óculos meos rem iniústam: * faciéntes prævaricatiónes odívi.

content.latin: 100:4 Non adhǽsit mihi cor pravum: * declinántem a me malígnum non cognoscébam.
content.english: 100:4 The perverse heart did not cleave to me: * and the malignant, that turned aside from me, I would not know.

segments.t: Non adhǽsit mihi cor pravum: * declinántem a me malígnum non cognoscébam.

content.latin: 100:5 Detrahéntem secréto próximo suo, * hunc persequébar.
content.english: 100:5 The man that in private detracted his neighbour, * him did I persecute.

segments.t: Detrahéntem secréto próximo suo, * hunc persequébar.

content.latin: 100:5 Supérbo óculo, et insatiábili corde, * cum hoc non edébam.
content.english: 100:5 With him that had a proud eye, and an unsatiable heart, * I would not eat.

segments.t: Supérbo óculo, et insatiábili corde, * cum hoc non edébam.

content.latin: 100:6 Óculi mei ad fidéles terræ ut sédeant mecum: * ámbulans in via immaculáta, hic mihi ministrábat.
content.english: 100:6 My eyes were upon the faithful of the earth, to sit with me: * the man that walked in the perfect way, he served me.

segments.t: Óculi mei ad fidéles terræ ut sédeant mecum: * ámbulans in via immaculáta, hic mihi ministrábat.

content.latin: 100:7 Non habitábit in médio domus meæ qui facit supérbiam: * qui lóquitur iníqua, non diréxit in conspéctu oculórum meórum.
content.english: 100:7 He that worketh pride shall not dwell in the midst of my house: * he that speaketh unjust things did not prosper before my eyes.

segments.t: Non habitábit in médio domus meæ qui facit supérbiam: * qui lóquitur iníqua, non diréxit in conspéctu oculórum meórum.

content.latin: 100:8 In matutíno interficiébam omnes peccatóres terræ: * ut dispérderem de civitáte Dómini omnes operántes iniquitátem.
content.english: 100:8 In the morning I put to death all the wicked of the land: * that I might cut off all the workers of iniquity from the city of the Lord.

segments.t: In matutíno interficiébam omnes peccatóres terræ: * ut dispérderem de civitáte Dómini omnes operántes iniquitátem.

content.english: 16:21 Woe be to the nation that riseth up against my people: for the Lord almighty will take revenge on them, * in the day of judgment he will visit them.

content.english: 145:2 Praise the Lord, O my soul, in my life I will praise the Lord: * I will sing to my God as long as I shall be.

segments.t: Lauda, ánima mea, Dóminum, laudábo Dóminum in vita mea: * psallam Deo meo quámdiu fúero.

content.english: 145:2 Put not your trust in princes: * in the children of men, in whom there is no salvation.

segments.t: Nolíte confídere in princípibus: * in fíliis hóminum, in quibus non est salus.

content.english: 145:4 His spirit shall go forth, and he shall return into his earth: * in that day all their thoughts shall perish.

segments.t: Exíbit spíritus eius, et revertétur in terram suam: * in illa die períbunt omnes cogitatiónes eórum.

content.english: 145:5 Blessed is he who hath the God of Jacob for his helper, whose hope is in the Lord his God: * who made heaven and earth, the sea, and all things that are in them.

segments.t: Beátus, cuius Deus Iacob adiútor eius, spes eius in Dómino, Deo ipsíus: * qui fecit cælum et terram, mare, et ómnia, quæ in eis sunt.

content.latin: 145:7 Qui custódit veritátem in sǽculum, facit iudícium iniúriam patiéntibus: * dat escam esuriéntibus.
content.english: 145:7 Who keepeth truth for ever: who executeth judgment for them that suffer wrong: * who giveth food to the hungry.

segments.t: Qui custódit veritátem in sǽculum, facit iudícium iniúriam patiéntibus: * dat escam esuriéntibus.

content.latin: 145:7 Dóminus solvit compedítos: * Dóminus illúminat cæcos.
content.english: 145:7 The Lord looseth them that are fettered: * the Lord enlighteneth the blind.

segments.t: Dóminus solvit compedítos: * Dóminus illúminat cæcos.

content.latin: 145:8 Dóminus érigit elísos, * Dóminus díligit iustos.
content.english: 145:8 The Lord lifteth up them that are cast down: * the Lord loveth the just.

segments.t: Dóminus érigit elísos, * Dóminus díligit iustos.

content.latin: 145:9 Dóminus custódit ádvenas, pupíllum et víduam suscípiet: * et vias peccatórum dispérdet.
content.english: 145:9 The Lord keepeth the strangers, he will support the fatherless and the widow: * and the ways of sinners he will destroy.

segments.t: Dóminus custódit ádvenas, pupíllum et víduam suscípiet: * et vias peccatórum dispérdet.

content.latin: 145:10 Regnábit Dóminus in sǽcula, Deus tuus, Sion, * in generatiónem et generatiónem.
content.english: 145:10 The Lord shall reign for ever: thy God, O Sion, * unto generation and generation.

segments.t: Regnábit Dóminus in sǽcula, Deus tuus, Sion, * in generatiónem et generatiónem.

content.english: 1:70 As he spoke by the mouth of his holy Prophets, * who are from the beginning:

segments.t: Sicut locútus est per os sanctórum, * qui a sǽculo sunt, prophetárum eius:

content.english: 1:71 Salvation from our enemies, * and from the hand of all that hate us:

content.english: 1:72 To perform mercy to our fathers, * and to remember his holy testament,

segments.t: Ad faciéndam misericórdiam cum pátribus nostris: * et memorári testaménti sui sancti.

content.latin: 1:75 In sanctitáte, et iustítia coram ipso, * ómnibus diébus nostris.

segments.t: In sanctitáte, et iustítia coram ipso, * ómnibus diébus nostris.

segments.t: Et tu, puer, Prophéta Altíssimi vocáberis: * præíbis enim ante fáciem Dómini, paráre vias eius:

content.latin: 1:77 Ad dandam sciéntiam salútis plebi eius: * in remissiónem peccatórum eórum:
content.english: 1:77 To give knowledge of salvation to his people, * unto the remission of their sins:

segments.t: Ad dandam sciéntiam salútis plebi eius: * in remissiónem peccatórum eórum:

content.latin: 1:78 Per víscera misericórdiæ Dei nostri: * in quibus visitávit nos, óriens ex alto:

content.latin: Nos servet a nocéntibus.
content.english: In all the deeds this day shall see.

content.latin: Linguam refrénans témperet,
content.english: May fear of him our tongues restrain,

content.latin: Ne litis horror ínsonet:
content.english: Lest strife unguarded speech should stain:

content.latin: Visum fovéndo cóntegat,
content.english: His favouring care our guardian be,

content.latin: Ne vanitátes háuriat.
content.english: Lest our eyes feed on vanity.

content.latin: Sint pura cordis íntima,
content.english: May every heart be pure from sin

content.latin: Absístat et vecórdia;
content.english: And folly find no place therein:

content.latin: Carnis terat supérbiam
content.english: Scant need of food, excess denied,

content.latin: Potus cibíque párcitas.
content.english: Wear down in us the body's pride.

content.latin: Ut, cum dies abscésserit,
content.english: That when the light of day is gone,

content.latin: Noctémque sors redúxerit,
content.english: And night in course shall follow on.

content.latin: Mundi per abstinéntiam
content.english: We, free from cares the world affords,

content.english: Psalm 25 [1]

segments.t: Psalmus 25

content.latin: 25:1 Iúdica me, Dómine, quóniam ego in innocéntia mea ingréssus sum: * et in Dómino sperans non infirmábor.
content.english: 25:1 Judge me, O Lord, for I have walked in my innocence: * and I have put my trust in the Lord, and shall not be weakened.

segments.t: Iúdica me, Dómine, quóniam ego in innocéntia mea ingréssus sum: * et in Dómino sperans non infirmábor.

content.latin: 25:2 Proba me, Dómine, et tenta me: * ure renes meos et cor meum.
content.english: 25:2 Prove me, O Lord, and try me; * burn my reins and my heart.

segments.t: Proba me, Dómine, et tenta me: * ure renes meos et cor meum.

content.latin: 25:3 Quóniam misericórdia tua ante óculos meos est: * et complácui in veritáte tua.
content.english: 25:3 For thy mercy is before my eyes; * and I am well pleased with thy truth.

segments.t: Quóniam misericórdia tua ante óculos meos est: * et complácui in veritáte tua.

content.latin: 25:4 Non sedi cum concílio vanitátis: * et cum iníqua geréntibus non introíbo.
content.english: 25:4 I have not sat with the council of vanity: * neither will I go in with the doers of unjust things.

segments.t: Non sedi cum concílio vanitátis: * et cum iníqua geréntibus non introíbo.

content.latin: 25:5 Odívi ecclésiam malignántium: * et cum ímpiis non sedébo.
content.english: 25:5 I have hated the assembly of the malignant; * and with the wicked I will not sit.

segments.t: Odívi ecclésiam malignántium: * et cum ímpiis non sedébo.

content.latin: 25:6 Lavábo inter innocéntes manus meas: * et circúmdabo altáre tuum, Dómine:
content.english: 25:6 I will wash my hands among the innocent; * and will compass thy altar, O Lord:

segments.t: Lavábo inter innocéntes manus meas: * et circúmdabo altáre tuum, Dómine:

content.latin: 25:7 Ut áudiam vocem laudis, * et enárrem univérsa mirabília tua.
content.english: 25:7 That I may hear the voice of thy praise: * and tell of all thy wondrous works.

segments.t: Ut áudiam vocem laudis, * et enárrem univérsa mirabília tua.

content.latin: 25:8 Dómine, diléxi decórem domus tuæ, * et locum habitatiónis glóriæ tuæ.
content.english: 25:8 I have loved, O Lord, the beauty of thy house; * and the place where thy glory dwelleth.

segments.t: Dómine, diléxi decórem domus tuæ, * et locum habitatiónis glóriæ tuæ.

content.latin: 25:9 Ne perdas cum ímpiis, Deus, ánimam meam, * et cum viris sánguinum vitam meam:
content.english: 25:9 Take not away my soul, O God, with the wicked: * nor my life with bloody men:

segments.t: Ne perdas cum ímpiis, Deus, ánimam meam, * et cum viris sánguinum vitam meam:

content.latin: 25:10 In quorum mánibus iniquitátes sunt: * déxtera eórum repléta est munéribus.
content.english: 25:10 In whose hands are iniquities: * their right hand is filled with gifts.

segments.t: In quorum mánibus iniquitátes sunt: * déxtera eórum repléta est munéribus.

content.latin: 25:11 Ego autem in innocéntia mea ingréssus sum: * rédime me, et miserére mei.
content.english: 25:11 But as for me, I have walked in my innocence: * redeem me, and have mercy on me.

segments.t: Ego autem in innocéntia mea ingréssus sum: * rédime me, et miserére mei.

content.latin: 25:12 Pes meus stetit in dirécto: * in ecclésiis benedícam te, Dómine.
content.english: 25:12 My foot hath stood in the direct way: * in the churches I will bless thee, O Lord.

segments.t: Pes meus stetit in dirécto: * in ecclésiis benedícam te, Dómine.

content.latin: Psalmus 51 [2]
content.english: Psalm 51 [2]

segments.t: Psalmus 51

content.latin: 51:3 Quid gloriáris in malítia, * qui potens es in iniquitáte?
content.english: 51:3 Why dost thou glory in malice, * thou that art mighty in iniquity?

segments.t: Quid gloriáris in malítia, * qui potens es in iniquitáte?

content.latin: 51:4 Tota die iniustítiam cogitávit lingua tua: * sicut novácula acúta fecísti dolum.
content.english: 51:4 All the day long thy tongue hath devised injustice: * as a sharp razor, thou hast wrought deceit.

segments.t: Tota die iniustítiam cogitávit lingua tua: * sicut novácula acúta fecísti dolum.

content.latin: 51:5 Dilexísti malítiam super benignitátem: * iniquitátem magis quam loqui æquitátem.
content.english: 51:5 Thou hast loved malice more than goodness: * and iniquity rather than to speak righteousness.

segments.t: Dilexísti malítiam super benignitátem: * iniquitátem magis quam loqui æquitátem.

content.latin: 51:6 Dilexísti ómnia verba præcipitatiónis, * lingua dolósa.
content.english: 51:6 Thou hast loved all the words of ruin, * O deceitful tongue.

segments.t: Dilexísti ómnia verba præcipitatiónis, * lingua dolósa.

content.latin: 51:7 Proptérea Deus déstruet te in finem, * evéllet te, et emigrábit te de tabernáculo tuo: et radícem tuam de terra vivéntium.
content.english: 51:7 Therefore will God destroy thee for ever: * he will pluck thee out, and remove thee from thy dwelling place: and thy root out of the land of the living.

segments.t: Proptérea Deus déstruet te in finem, * evéllet te, et emigrábit te de tabernáculo tuo: et radícem tuam de terra vivéntium.

content.latin: 51:8 Vidébunt iusti, et timébunt, et super eum ridébunt, et dicent: * Ecce homo, qui non pósuit Deum adiutórem suum:
content.english: 51:8 The just shall see and fear, and shall laugh at him, and say: * Behold the man that made not God his helper:

segments.t: Vidébunt iusti, et timébunt, et super eum ridébunt, et dicent: * Ecce homo, qui non pósuit Deum adiutórem suum:

content.latin: 51:9 Sed sperávit in multitúdine divitiárum suárum: * et præváluit in vanitáte sua.
content.english: 51:9 But trusted in the abundance of his riches: * and prevailed in his vanity.

segments.t: Sed sperávit in multitúdine divitiárum suárum: * et præváluit in vanitáte sua.

content.latin: 51:10 Ego autem, sicut olíva fructífera in domo Dei, * sperávi in misericórdia Dei in ætérnum: et in sǽculum sǽculi.
content.english: 51:10 But I, as a fruitful olive tree in the house of God, * have hoped in the mercy of God for ever, yea for ever and ever.

segments.t: Ego autem, sicut olíva fructífera in domo Dei, * sperávi in misericórdia Dei in ætérnum: et in sǽculum sǽculi.

content.latin: 51:11 Confitébor tibi in sǽculum, quia fecísti: * et exspectábo nomen tuum, quóniam bonum est in conspéctu sanctórum tuórum.
content.english: 51:11 I will praise thee for ever, because thou hast done it: * and I will wait on thy name, for it is good in the sight of thy saints.

segments.t: Confitébor tibi in sǽculum, quia fecísti: * et exspectábo nomen tuum, quóniam bonum est in conspéctu sanctórum tuórum.

content.english: Psalm 52 [3]

segments.t: Psalmus 52

content.latin: 52:1 Dixit insípiens in corde suo: * Non est Deus.
content.english: 52:1 The fool said in his heart: * There is no God.

segments.t: Dixit insípiens in corde suo: * Non est Deus.

content.latin: 52:2 Corrúpti sunt, et abominábiles facti sunt in iniquitátibus: * non est qui fáciat bonum.
content.english: 52:2 They are corrupted, and become abominable in iniquities: * there is none that doth good.

segments.t: Corrúpti sunt, et abominábiles facti sunt in iniquitátibus: * non est qui fáciat bonum.

content.latin: 52:3 Deus de cælo prospéxit super fílios hóminum: * ut vídeat si est intéllegens, aut requírens Deum.
content.english: 52:3 God looked down from heaven on the children of men: * to see if there were any that did understand, or did seek God.

segments.t: Deus de cælo prospéxit super fílios hóminum: * ut vídeat si est intéllegens, aut requírens Deum.

content.latin: 52:4 Omnes declinavérunt, simul inútiles facti sunt: * non est qui fáciat bonum, non est usque ad unum.
content.english: 52:4 All have gone aside, they are become unprofitable together, * there is none that doth good, no not one.

segments.t: Omnes declinavérunt, simul inútiles facti sunt: * non est qui fáciat bonum, non est usque ad unum.

content.latin: 52:5 Nonne scient omnes qui operántur iniquitátem, * qui dévorant plebem meam ut cibum panis?
content.english: 52:5 Shall not all the workers of iniquity know, * who eat up my people as they eat bread?

segments.t: Nonne scient omnes qui operántur iniquitátem, * qui dévorant plebem meam ut cibum panis?

content.latin: 52:6 Deum non invocavérunt: * illic trepidavérunt timóre, ubi non erat timor.
content.english: 52:6 They have not called upon God: * there have they trembled for fear, where there was no fear.

segments.t: Deum non invocavérunt: * illic trepidavérunt timóre, ubi non erat timor.

content.latin: 52:6 Quóniam Deus dissipávit ossa eórum qui homínibus placent: * confúsi sunt, quóniam Deus sprevit eos.
content.english: 52:6 For God hath scattered the bones of them that please men: * they have been confounded, because God hath despised them.

segments.t: Quóniam Deus dissipávit ossa eórum qui homínibus placent: * confúsi sunt, quóniam Deus sprevit eos.

content.latin: 52:7 Quis dabit ex Sion salutáre Israël? * cum convérterit Deus captivitátem plebis suæ, exsultábit Iacob, et lætábitur Israël.
content.english: 52:7 Who will give out of Sion the salvation of Israel? * when God shall bring back the captivity of his people, Jacob shall rejoice, and Israel shall be glad.

segments.t: Quis dabit ex Sion salutáre Israël? * cum convérterit Deus captivitátem plebis suæ, exsultábit Iacob, et lætábitur Israël.

content.latin: Dómine Deus omnípotens, qui ad princípium huius diéi nos perveníre fecísti: tua nos hódie salva virtúte; ut in hac die ad nullum declinémus peccátum, sed semper ad tuam iustítiam faciéndam nostra procédant elóquia, dirigántur cogitatiónes et ópera.
content.english: O Lord, our heavenly Father, Almighty and everlasting God, who has safely brought us to the beginning of this day: defend us by thy mighty power; and grant that this day we fall into no sin, but that all our doings may be ordered by thy governance, to do always what is righteous in thy sight.

content.latin: Per Dóminum nostrum Iesum Christum, Fílium tuum: qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitáte Spíritus Sancti, Deus, per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum.
content.english: Through Jesus Christ, thy Son our Lord, Who liveth and reigneth with thee, in the unity of the Holy Ghost, God, world without end.

content.latin: Undécimo Kaléndas Novémbris Luna undécima Anno Dómini 2026
content.english: October 22nd 2026, the 11th day of the Moon, were born into the better life:

content.latin: Hierosólymis sanctæ Maríæ Salóme, matris sanctórum Iacóbi et Ioánnis Apostolórum, quæ in Evangélio légitur circa Dómini sepultúram sollícita.
content.english: At Jerusalem, the blessed Bishop Mark, a man of great eminence and learning, who was the first Gentile to be entrusted with the government of the Church of Jerusalem, and who in no long time gained the palm of martyrdom under the Emperor Antonine.

content.latin: Item Hierosólymis beáti Marci Epíscopi, claríssimi et doctíssimi viri, qui primus ex Géntibus Ecclésiam Hierosolymórum suscépit regéndam, ac, non multo post, sub Antoníno Imperatóre, martýrii méruit palmam.
content.english: At Adrianople, in Thrace, the holy martyrs Philip, Bishop (of Heraclea,) the Priest Severus, Eusebius, and Hermes, who, under the Emperor Julian the Apostate, were imprisoned and flogged, and then burnt.

content.latin: Hadrianópoli, in Thrácia, natális sanctórum Mártyrum Philíppi Epíscopi, Sevéri Presbýteri, Eusébii et Hermétis; qui, sub Iuliáno Apóstata, post cárceres et flagélla, incéndio cremáti sunt.
content.english: Likewise, the holy martyrs the Bishop Alexander, the soldier Heraclius, and their Companions.

content.latin: Item sanctórum Mártyrum Alexándri Epíscopi, Heráclii mílitis, et Sociórum.
content.english: At Fermo, in the March of Ancona, (in the third century,) the holy Bishop and martyr Philip.

content.latin: Apud Firmum, in Picéno, natális sancti Philíppi, Epíscopi et Mártyris.
content.english: At Huesca, in Spain, (in the ninth century,) the holy sisters Nunilo and Alodia, two Virgins who were punished with death by the Saracens for their confession of the faith, and so suffered martyrdom.

content.latin: Apud Colóniam Agrippínam sanctæ Córdulæ, quæ, cum esset una ex sodálibus sanctæ Ursulæ, atque aliárum supplíciis et cǽdibus pertérrita se occultásset, postrídie, eius rei pǽnitens, se ultro patefécit Hunnis, et, novíssima ómnium, martýrii corónam accépit.
content.english: At Cologne, holy Cordula, one of the Companions of holy Ursula, who had hidden herself in terror at the sight of the sufferings and slaughter of the others, but repented thereof, and on the next day showed herself openly, and received the crown of martyrdom, the last of them all.

content.latin: Oscæ, in Hispánia, sanctárum Vírginum Nunilónis et Alódiæ sorórum, quæ, a Saracénis ob fídei confessiónem capitáli senténtia punítæ, martýrium consummárunt.
content.english: At Hierapolis, in Phrygia, holy Abercius, who was illustrious in the time of the Emperor Mark Antonine.

content.latin: Hierápoli, in Phrýgia, sancti Abércii Epíscopi, qui sub Marco Antoníno Imperatóre cláruit.
content.english: At Rouen, holy Melanius, Bishop (of that see,) who was ordained by holy Pope Stephen I., and sent thither to preach the Gospel.

content.latin: Rotómagi sancti Melánii Epíscopi, qui, a sancto Stéphano Papa ordinátus, illuc ad prædicándum Evangélium missus est.
content.english: In Tuscany, (towards the end of the ninth century,) the holy Irishman Donatus, (Bishop of Fiesole.)

content.latin: In Túscia sancti Donáti Scoti, Epíscopi Fæsuláni.
content.english: At Verona, (in the sixth century,) the holy Confessor Verecundus, Bishop (of that see.)

content.latin: Verónæ sancti Verecúndi, Epíscopi et Confessóris.
content.english: At Jerusalem, the holy Mary Salome, concerning whom it is written in the Gospel that she was careful about the burying of the Lord.

content.latin: ℣. Et álibi aliórum plurimórum sanctórum Mártyrum et Confessórum, atque sanctárum Vírginum.
content.english: ℣. And elsewhere many other holy martyrs, confessors, and holy virgins.

segments.t: Et álibi aliórum plurimórum sanctórum Mártyrum et Confessórum, atque sanctárum Vírginum.

content.english: Our Father is said silently until And lead us not into temptation:.

segments.t: Pater Noster dicitur secreto usque ad Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:

content.latin: Pater noster, qui es in cælis, sanctificétur nomen tuum: advéniat regnum tuum: fiat volúntas tua, sicut in cælo et in terra. Panem nostrum cotidiánum da nobis hódie: et dimítte nobis débita nostra, sicut et nos dimíttimus debitóribus nostris:
content.english: Our Father, who art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name. Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done on earth as it is in heaven. Give us this day our daily bread. And forgive us our trespasses, as we forgive those who trespass against us.

content.latin: ℣. Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:
content.english: ℣. And lead us not into temptation:

segments.t: Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:

content.latin: ℟. Sed líbera nos a malo.
content.english: ℟. But deliver us from evil.

segments.t: Sed líbera nos a malo.

content.latin: ℣. Réspice in servos tuos, Dómine, et in ópera tua, et dírige fílios eórum.
content.english: ℣. Look upon thy servants and upon thy works: and direct their children.

segments.t: Réspice in servos tuos, Dómine, et in ópera tua, et dírige fílios eórum.

content.latin: ℟. Et sit splendor Dómini Dei nostri super nos, et ópera mánuum nostrárum dírige super nos, et opus mánuum nostrárum dírige.
content.english: ℟. And let the brightness of the Lord our God be upon us. Direct thou the works of our hands; yea, the work of our hands do thou direct.

segments.t: Et sit splendor Dómini Dei nostri super nos, et ópera mánuum nostrárum dírige super nos, et opus mánuum nostrárum dírige.

content.latin: Orémus.
content.english: Let us pray.

content.latin: Dirígere et sanctificáre, régere et gubernáre dignáre, Dómine Deus, Rex cæli et terræ, hódie corda et córpora nostra, sensus, sermónes et actus nostros in lege tua, et in opéribus mandatórum tuórum: ut hic et in ætérnum, te auxiliánte, salvi et líberi esse mereámur, Salvátor mundi: Qui vivis et regnas in sǽcula sæculórum.
content.english: O Lord, Almighty God, King of heaven and earth, Saviour of the world, bless, lead, rule and govern our hearts and bodies, our senses, words and deeds today, following thy law and commandments, that here and for eternity with thy help we shall be saved in freedom. Who livest and reignest, world without end.

content.english: ℟. Amen.

content.latin: 53:3 Deus, in nómine tuo salvum me fac: * et in virtúte tua iúdica me.
content.english: 53:3 Save me, O God, by thy name, * and judge me in thy strength.

segments.t: Deus, in nómine tuo salvum me fac: * et in virtúte tua iúdica me.

content.latin: 53:4 Deus, exáudi oratiónem meam: * áuribus pércipe verba oris mei.
content.english: 53:4 O God, hear my prayer: * give ear to the words of my mouth.

segments.t: Deus, exáudi oratiónem meam: * áuribus pércipe verba oris mei.

content.latin: 53:5 Quóniam aliéni insurrexérunt advérsum me, et fortes quæsiérunt ánimam meam: * et non proposuérunt Deum ante conspéctum suum.
content.english: 53:5 For strangers have risen up against me; and the mighty have sought after my soul: * and they have not set God before their eyes.

segments.t: Quóniam aliéni insurrexérunt advérsum me, et fortes quæsiérunt ánimam meam: * et non proposuérunt Deum ante conspéctum suum.

content.latin: 53:6 Ecce enim, Deus ádiuvat me: * et Dóminus suscéptor est ánimæ meæ.
content.english: 53:6 For behold God is my helper: * and the Lord is the protector of my soul.

segments.t: Ecce enim, Deus ádiuvat me: * et Dóminus suscéptor est ánimæ meæ.

content.latin: 53:7 Avérte mala inimícis meis: * et in veritáte tua dispérde illos.
content.english: 53:7 Turn back the evils upon my enemies; * and cut them off in thy truth.

segments.t: Avérte mala inimícis meis: * et in veritáte tua dispérde illos.

content.latin: 53:8 Voluntárie sacrificábo tibi, * et confitébor nómini tuo, Dómine: quóniam bonum est:
content.english: 53:8 I will freely sacrifice to thee, * and will give praise, O God, to thy name: because it is good:

segments.t: Voluntárie sacrificábo tibi, * et confitébor nómini tuo, Dómine: quóniam bonum est:

content.latin: 53:9 Quóniam ex omni tribulatióne eripuísti me: * et super inimícos meos despéxit óculus meus.
content.english: 53:9 For thou hast delivered me out of all trouble: * and my eye hath looked down upon my enemies.

segments.t: Quóniam ex omni tribulatióne eripuísti me: * et super inimícos meos despéxit óculus meus.

segments.t: Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
Psalmus 54(2-16)

content.latin: 54:2 Exáudi, Deus, oratiónem meam, et ne despéxeris deprecatiónem meam: * inténde mihi, et exáudi me.
content.english: 54:2 Hear, O God, my prayer, and despise not my supplication: * be attentive to me and hear me.

segments.t: Exáudi, Deus, oratiónem meam, et ne despéxeris deprecatiónem meam: * inténde mihi, et exáudi me.

content.latin: 54:3 Contristátus sum in exercitatióne mea: * et conturbátus sum a voce inimíci, et a tribulatióne peccatóris.
content.english: 54:3 I am grieved in my exercise; * and am troubled, at the voice of the enemy, and at the tribulation of the sinner.

segments.t: Contristátus sum in exercitatióne mea: * et conturbátus sum a voce inimíci, et a tribulatióne peccatóris.

content.latin: 54:4 Quóniam declinavérunt in me iniquitátes: * et in ira molésti erant mihi.
content.english: 54:4 For they have cast iniquities upon me; * and in wrath they were troublesome to me.

segments.t: Quóniam declinavérunt in me iniquitátes: * et in ira molésti erant mihi.

content.latin: 54:5 Cor meum conturbátum est in me: * et formído mortis cécidit super me.
content.english: 54:5 My heart is troubled within me: * and the fear of death is fallen upon me.

segments.t: Cor meum conturbátum est in me: * et formído mortis cécidit super me.

content.latin: 54:6 Timor et tremor venérunt super me: * et contexérunt me ténebræ.
content.english: 54:6 Fear and trembling are come upon me: * and darkness hath covered me.

segments.t: Timor et tremor venérunt super me: * et contexérunt me ténebræ.

content.latin: 54:7 Et dixi: Quis dabit mihi pennas sicut colúmbæ, * et volábo, et requiéscam?
content.english: 54:7 And I said: Who will give me wings like a dove, * and I will fly and be at rest?

segments.t: Et dixi: Quis dabit mihi pennas sicut colúmbæ, * et volábo, et requiéscam?

content.latin: 54:8 Ecce, elongávi fúgiens: * et mansi in solitúdine.
content.english: 54:8 Lo, I have gone far off flying away; * and I abode in the wilderness.

segments.t: Ecce, elongávi fúgiens: * et mansi in solitúdine.

content.latin: 54:9 Exspectábam eum, qui salvum me fecit * a pusillanimitáte spíritus et tempestáte.
content.english: 54:9 I waited for him that hath saved me * from pusillanimity of spirit, and a storm.

segments.t: Exspectábam eum, qui salvum me fecit * a pusillanimitáte spíritus et tempestáte.

content.latin: 54:10 Præcípita, Dómine, dívide linguas eórum: * quóniam vidi iniquitátem, et contradictiónem in civitáte.
content.english: 54:10 Cast down, O Lord, and divide their tongues; * for I have seen iniquity and contradiction in the city.

segments.t: Præcípita, Dómine, dívide linguas eórum: * quóniam vidi iniquitátem, et contradictiónem in civitáte.

content.latin: 54:11 Die ac nocte circúmdabit eam super muros eius iníquitas: * et labor in médio eius, et iniustítia.
content.english: 54:11 Day and night shall iniquity surround it upon its walls: * and in the midst thereof are labour, and injustice.

segments.t: Die ac nocte circúmdabit eam super muros eius iníquitas: * et labor in médio eius, et iniustítia.

content.latin: 54:12 Et non defécit de platéis eius * usúra, et dolus.
content.english: 54:12 And usury and deceit * have not departed from its streets.

segments.t: Et non defécit de platéis eius * usúra, et dolus.

content.latin: 54:13 Quóniam si inimícus meus maledixísset mihi, * sustinuíssem útique.
content.english: 54:13 For if my enemy had reviled me, * I would verily have borne with it.

segments.t: Quóniam si inimícus meus maledixísset mihi, * sustinuíssem útique.

content.latin: 54:13 Et si is, qui óderat me, super me magna locútus fuísset, * abscondíssem me fórsitan ab eo.
content.english: 54:13 And if he that hated me had spoken great things against me, * I would perhaps have hidden myself from him.

segments.t: Et si is, qui óderat me, super me magna locútus fuísset, * abscondíssem me fórsitan ab eo.

content.latin: 54:14 Tu vero, homo unánimis: * dux meus, et notus meus:
content.english: 54:14 But thou a man of one mind, * my guide, and my familiar.

segments.t: Tu vero, homo unánimis: * dux meus, et notus meus:

content.latin: 54:15 Qui simul mecum dulces capiébas cibos: * in domo Dei ambulávimus cum consénsu.
content.english: 54:15 Who didst take sweetmeats together with me: * in the house of God we walked with consent.

segments.t: Qui simul mecum dulces capiébas cibos: * in domo Dei ambulávimus cum consénsu.

content.latin: 54:16 Véniat mors super illos: * et descéndant in inférnum vivéntes:
content.english: 54:16 Let death come upon them, * and let them go down alive into hell.

segments.t: Véniat mors super illos: * et descéndant in inférnum vivéntes:

content.latin: 54:16 Quóniam nequítiæ in habitáculis eórum: * in médio eórum.
content.english: 54:16 For there is wickedness in their dwellings: * in the midst of them.

segments.t: Quóniam nequítiæ in habitáculis eórum: * in médio eórum.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

segments.t: Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.

content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

Psalmus 54(17-24)

content.latin: 54:17 Ego autem ad Deum clamávi: * et Dóminus salvábit me.
content.english: 54:17 But I have cried to God: * and the Lord will save me.

segments.t: Ego autem ad Deum clamávi: * et Dóminus salvábit me.

content.latin: 54:18 Véspere, et mane, et merídie narrábo et annuntiábo: * et exáudiet vocem meam.
content.english: 54:18 Evening and morning, and at noon I will speak and declare: * and he shall hear my voice.

segments.t: Véspere, et mane, et merídie narrábo et annuntiábo: * et exáudiet vocem meam.

content.latin: 54:19 Rédimet in pace ánimam meam ab his, qui appropínquant mihi: * quóniam inter multos erant mecum.
content.english: 54:19 He shall redeem my soul in peace from them that draw near to me: * for among many they were with me.

segments.t: Rédimet in pace ánimam meam ab his, qui appropínquant mihi: * quóniam inter multos erant mecum.

content.latin: 54:20 Exáudiet Deus, et humiliábit illos, * qui est ante sǽcula.
content.english: 54:20 God shall hear, * and the Eternal shall humble them.

segments.t: Exáudiet Deus, et humiliábit illos, * qui est ante sǽcula.

content.latin: 54:20 Non enim est illis commutátio, et non timuérunt Deum: * exténdit manum suam in retribuéndo.
content.english: 54:20 For there is no change with them, and they have not feared God: * he hath stretched forth his hand to repay.

segments.t: Non enim est illis commutátio, et non timuérunt Deum: * exténdit manum suam in retribuéndo.

content.latin: 54:21 Contaminavérunt testaméntum eius, divísi sunt ab ira vultus eius: * et appropinquávit cor illíus.
content.english: 54:21 They have defiled his covenant, they are divided by the wrath of his countenance, * and his heart hath drawn near.

segments.t: Contaminavérunt testaméntum eius, divísi sunt ab ira vultus eius: * et appropinquávit cor illíus.

content.latin: 54:22 Mollíti sunt sermónes eius super óleum: * et ipsi sunt iácula.
content.english: 54:22 His words are smoother than oil, * and the same are darts.

segments.t: Mollíti sunt sermónes eius super óleum: * et ipsi sunt iácula.

content.latin: 54:23 Iacta super Dóminum curam tuam, et ipse te enútriet: * non dabit in ætérnum fluctuatiónem iusto.
content.english: 54:23 Cast thy care upon the Lord, and he shall sustain thee: * he shall not suffer the just to waver for ever.

segments.t: Iacta super Dóminum curam tuam, et ipse te enútriet: * non dabit in ætérnum fluctuatiónem iusto.

content.latin: 54:24 Tu vero, Deus, dedúces eos, * in púteum intéritus.
content.english: 54:24 But thou, O God, shalt bring them down * into the pit of destruction.

segments.t: Tu vero, Deus, dedúces eos, * in púteum intéritus.

content.latin: 54:24 Viri sánguinum, et dolósi non dimidiábunt dies suos: * ego autem sperábo in te, Dómine.
content.english: 54:24 Bloody and deceitful men shall not live out half their days; * but I will trust in thee, O Lord.

segments.t: Viri sánguinum, et dolósi non dimidiábunt dies suos: * ego autem sperábo in te, Dómine.

content.english: Ant. For behold God is my helper: and the Lord is the protector of my soul.

Deus ádiuvat me: et Dóminus suscéptor est ánimæ meæ.

content.latin: Fratres: Qui gloriátur, in Dómino gloriétur. Non enim qui seípsum comméndat, ille probátus est; sed quem Deus comméndat.
content.english: Brothers: But he that glorieth, let him glory in the Lord. For not he who commendeth himself, is approved, but he, whom God commendeth.

content.latin: ℟. Deo grátias.
content.english: ℟. Thanks be to God.

segments.t: Deo grátias.

content.latin: ℟.br. Spécie tua * Et pulchritúdine tua.
content.english: ℟.br. In thy comeliness * and in thy beauty.

segments.t: ℟.br.
Spécie tua * Et pulchritúdine tua.

content.latin: ℟. Spécie tua * Et pulchritúdine tua.
content.english: ℟. In thy comeliness * and in thy beauty.

segments.t: Spécie tua * Et pulchritúdine tua.

content.latin: ℣. Inténde, próspere procéde, et regna.
content.english: ℣. Go forward, fare prosperously, and reign.

segments.t: Inténde, próspere procéde, et regna.

segments.t: Spécie tua * Et pulchritúdine tua.

content.latin: ℣. Adiuvábit eam Deus vultu suo.
content.english: ℣. God shall help her with His countenance.

segments.t: Adiuvábit eam Deus vultu suo.

content.latin: ℟. Deus in médio eius, non commovébitur.
content.english: ℟. God is in the midst of her she shall not be moved.

segments.t: Deus in médio eius, non commovébitur.

content.latin: ℣. Dómine, exáudi oratiónem meam.
content.english: ℣. O Lord, hear my prayer.

segments.t: Dómine, exáudi oratiónem meam.

content.english: ℟. And let my cry come unto thee.

segments.t: Et clamor meus ad te véniat.

content.latin: Per Dóminum nostrum Iesum Christum, Fílium tuum: qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitáte Spíritus Sancti, Deus, per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum.
content.english: Through Jesus Christ, thy Son our Lord, Who liveth and reigneth with thee, in the unity of the Holy Ghost, God, world without end.

content.english: ℟. Amen.

content.english: ℣. Let us bless the Lord.

content.english: ℣. May the souls of the faithful, through the mercy of God, rest in peace.

content.english: ℟. Amen.
